title: GitLab patches critical unauthenticated RCE vulnerability across versions 7.0 through 19.5
summary: GitLab published emergency patch release 19.5.1 alongside backports down to version 18.11.13 to resolve CVE-2026-110264, a maximum-severity integer overflow in its regular expression compiler enabling unauthenticated remote code execution on self-managed servers.
research_notes:
Identify the current self-managed GitLab instance version by checking the administration dashboard or running gitlab-rake gitlab:env:info on the host.

Select the corresponding patch target for the active version line: upgrade 19.5.x to 19.5.1, 19.4.x to 19.4.3, 19.3.x to 19.3.6, 19.2.x to 19.2.9, 19.1.x to 19.1.9, 19.0.x to 19.0.10, or legacy 7.0 through 18.11.x to 18.11.13.

Execute the package manager update command or container image pull to apply the security patch, and restart GitLab services so updated binaries take effect.

Inspect Puma worker logs and application error logs for regular expression compiler errors or abnormal worker termination to detect past exploitation attempts.

Apply security releases immediately to internet-exposed self-managed GitLab instances because unauthenticated remote code execution requires no credentials or user interaction.

Upgrade directly to the designated patch release within the active minor version branch to avoid unnecessary database migrations and reduce service downtime.

Do not rely on perimeter web application firewall rules or configuration workarounds alone, as malicious regular expression patterns can be processed across various document rendering pathways.
